1	use ruff_text_size::{Ranged, TextLen, TextRange};
2	
3	use super::{TokenKind, Tokens};
4	use crate::{AnyNodeRef, ExprRef};
5	
6	/// Returns an iterator over the ranges of the optional parentheses surrounding an expression.
7	///
8	/// E.g. for `((f()))` with `f()` as expression, the iterator returns the ranges (1, 6) and (0, 7).
9	///
10	/// Note that without a parent the range can be inaccurate, e.g. `f(a)` we falsely return a set of
11	/// parentheses around `a` even if the parentheses actually belong to `f`. That is why you should
12	/// generally prefer [`parenthesized_range`].
13	pub fn parentheses_iterator<'a>(
14	    expr: ExprRef<'a>,
15	    parent: Option<AnyNodeRef>,
16	    tokens: &'a Tokens,
17	) -> impl Iterator<Item = TextRange> + 'a {
18	    let after_tokens = if let Some(parent) = parent {
19	        // If the parent is a node that brings its own parentheses, exclude the closing parenthesis
20	        // from our search range. Otherwise, we risk matching on calls, like `func(x)`, for which
21	        // the open and close parentheses are part of the `Arguments` node.
22	        let exclusive_parent_end = if parent.is_arguments() {
23	            parent.end() - ")".text_len()
24	        } else {
25	            parent.end()
26	        };
27	
28	        tokens.in_range(TextRange::new(expr.end(), exclusive_parent_end))
29	    } else {
30	        tokens.after(expr.end())
31	    };
32	
33	    let right_parens = after_tokens
34	        .iter()
35	        .filter(|token| !token.kind().is_trivia())
36	        .take_while(move |token| token.kind() == TokenKind::Rpar);
37	
38	    let left_parens = tokens
39	        .before(expr.start())
40	        .iter()
41	        .rev()
42	        .filter(|token| !token.kind().is_trivia())
43	        .take_while(|token| token.kind() == TokenKind::Lpar);
44	
45	    right_parens
46	        .zip(left_parens)
47	        .map(|(right, left)| TextRange::new(left.start(), right.end()))
48	}
49	
50	/// Returns the [`TextRange`] of a given expression including parentheses, if the expression is
51	/// parenthesized; or `None`, if the expression is not parenthesized.
52	pub fn parenthesized_range(
53	    expr: ExprRef,
54	    parent: AnyNodeRef,
55	    tokens: &Tokens,
56	) -> Option<TextRange> {
57	    parentheses_iterator(expr, Some(parent), tokens).last()
58	}

Otherwise, we risk matching on calls, like `func(x)`, for which\n        // the open and close parentheses are part of the `Arguments` node.\n        let exclusive_parent_end = if parent.is_arguments() {\n            parent.end() - \")\".text_len()\n        } else {\n            parent.end()\n        };\n\n        tokens.in_range(TextRange::new(expr.end(), exclusive_parent_end))\n    } else {\n        tokens.after(expr.end())\n    };\n\n    let right_parens = after_tokens\n        .iter()\n        .filter(|token| !token.kind().is_trivia())\n        .take_while(move |token| token.kind() == TokenKind::Rpar);\n\n    let left_parens = tokens\n        .before(expr.start())\n        .iter()\n        .rev()\n        .filter(|token| !token.kind().is_trivia())\n        .take_while(|token| token.kind() == TokenKind::Lpar);\n\n    right_parens\n        .zip(left_parens)\n        .map(|(right, left)| TextRange::new(left.start(), right.end()))\n}\n\n/// Returns the [`TextRange`] of a given expression including parentheses, if the expression is\n/// parenthesized; or `None`, if the expression is not parenthesized.\npub fn parenthesized_range(\n    expr: ExprRef,\n    parent: AnyNodeRef,\n    tokens: &Tokens,\n) -> Option<TextRange> {\n    parentheses_iterator(expr, Some(parent), tokens).last()\n}\n", "numLines": 59, "startLine": 1, "totalLines": 59}}

The implementation is complete. Here's a summary of what I did:

## Summary

The RUF050 rule replaces empty `if cond: pass` statements that have side effects with `cond` as a bare expression statement. The bug: a multiline condition with a **top-level line break** (a break not enclosed by the condition's own brackets) is only valid because the `if (...)` parentheses join the lines — lifting the raw `test.range()` slice into a standalone statement produces invalid Python.

### Changes to `crates/ruff_linter/src/rules/ruff/rules/unnecessary_if.rs`

1. **New helper `condition_has_top_level_line_break`** — walks the tokens within `test.range()`, tracking bracket depth (`(`/`[`/`{` increment, `)`/`]`/`}` decrement), and returns `true` if a `NonLogicalNewline`/`Newline` occurs at depth 0. Token-based scanning correctly ignores brackets/newlines inside string literals.

2. **Fix-generation logic** — three branches for the side-effect case:
   - **Walrus** (`x := ...`): wrap in parens (unchanged).
   - **Top-level line break**: use `parenthesized_range(test, stmt, tokens)` to grab the source range *including* the existing outer parens, so the expression stays valid (`unwrap_or(test.range())` as a safe fallback).
   - **Otherwise** (single-line, or multiline call whose breaks are inside its own parens): use the raw condition text with no added parens.

### Test fixture & snapshot
- Added two multiline cases to `RUF050.py`: a `foo() and bar()` wrapped in outer parens (→ parens preserved) and a multiline `foo(a, b,)` call (→ raw text kept).
- Regenerated the `.snap` file. Verified the test passes under `INSTA_UPDATE=no` (the verification setting).

The generated fixes confirm the intended behavior: case 1 emits `(\n    foo()\n    and bar()\n)` and case 2 emits `foo(\n    a,\n    b,\n)`.
